experiment_description: Device-independent two-point-measurement quantum-memory test on a trapped-ion processor. A chain of three ground-state-cooled 40Ca+ ions was confined in a macroscopic linear Paul trap. The two outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E, while the middle ion served only as a spacer to reduce optical cross-talk. Qubit manipulations used an individually addressed 729 nm quadrupole laser with linewidth below 1 Hz, incident at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis; single-ion addressing used a crossed acousto-optic-deflector setup. State readout used resonant 397 nm fluorescence collected onto an EMCCD camera. The two outer ions were initialized in a Bell state with a single Mølmer-Sørensen entangling gate. Qubit A′ was then measured at the first time point. A random variable X with alphabet {0,1,2,3} selected one of four Pauli measurements {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}; the binary first outcome was A. During this mid-circuit measurement, qubit E was spectroscopically decoupled by shelving it in unused D5/2 levels, followed by Doppler and polarization-gradient re-cooling. Qubit A was then re-prepared in a state depending only on A and not on X: the quantum-memory test used sigma_x eigenstates |+> and |-> as the two post-measurement states. A variable waiting time was inserted after the first measurement and before the two-qubit unitary; the displayed memory-decay experiment swept the wait time from 0 ms to 100 ms. Magnetic-field noise was mitigated with dynamical-decoupling echo pulses every 2.5 ms during the wait. The subsequent unitary consisted of a CNOT gate followed by a virtual full SWAP of the two qubit labels. The CNOT was implemented as R_C,0(pi/2) · R_T,pi(pi/2) · R_T,pi/4(pi) · MS_XX^{C,T}(pi/2) · R_T,pi/2(pi/2), where R_i,phi(theta) is a single-qubit equatorial rotation of qubit i by angle theta about phase phi, and MS_XX is a Mølmer-Sørensen XX interaction. The second-time binary measurement on qubit B was the observable (sigma_x+sigma_z)/sqrt(2). From the observed conditional probabilities Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), the classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was computed as the sum over b0,b1 of the infimum over x of the sum over a of Pr(A=a,B=b_a|X=x). The same probability data were also used to evaluate Pearl’s cross-talk witness Delta_Pr(AB|X), defined as the maximum over a of the sum over b of the supremum over x of Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x). Cross-talk was additionally addressed by estimating the average causal direct effect ACDE, the supremum over a,b,x,x′ of the absolute difference between Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x)=b) and Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x′)=b). The qubit-memory fidelity lower bound was inferred from Gamma_Pr(AB|X) using the paper’s device-independent qubit-memory bound.

temporal_correlation_gamma.description: Measured value of the two-point-measurement classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) for the optimized quantum-memory certification sequence with no added storage delay beyond the base sequence; classical memory models obey Gamma_Pr(AB|X) >= 1.

qubit_memory_fidelity_lower_bound_percen.description: Device-independent lower bound, in percent, on the fidelity of the implemented qubit memory channel to an ideal qubit memory channel inferred from the measured temporal correlations.

pearl_cross_talk_parameter.description: Measured Pearl-inequality parameter Delta_Pr(AB|X) obtained from the same optimized quantum-memory data; values above 1 would witness cross-talk influence.

average_causal_direct_effect.description: Measured average causal direct effect used to quantify direct cross-talk influence from the first measurement setting X to the second outcome B not mediated by A.

certified_quantum_memory_time_ms.description: Storage time over which the trapped-ion qubit memory was reported to be certified as quantum by the temporal-correlation protocol.

experiment_description: Two-point-measurement experiment testing non-classical quantum causal relations with a partial-swap interaction on the same three-ion 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor. The outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E and were initialized in a Bell state using a single Mølmer-Sørensen gate; the middle ion acted as a spacer. Individual control used the addressed 729 nm laser at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis, and fluorescence readout used 397 nm light and an EMCCD camera. At the first time point, qubit A′ was measured with X in {0,1,2,3} selecting the four Pauli observables {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}, yielding binary outcome A. Qubit E was shelved during the mid-circuit measurement to suppress measurement back-action, and the ion chain was re-cooled afterward. The post-measurement qubit A was prepared in a sigma_y eigenstate depending only on A and not on X: |+i> for one binary outcome and |-i> for the other, according to the paper’s post-processing convention. The two-qubit interaction was the partial-swap gate U_PS(alpha)=cos(alpha/2) id + i sin(alpha/2) U_swap, where alpha is the controlled swap angle in radians, id is the two-qubit identity, and U_swap is the full two-qubit swap operator. The experiment swept alpha from 0 to pi. In the trapped-ion circuit, U_PS(alpha) was implemented as MS_ZZ(-alpha/2) · MS_YY(-alpha/2) · MS_XX(-alpha/2), with the Mølmer-Sørensen rotation angle controlled through laser intensity while keeping gate time fixed. The second-time measurement on qubit B was sigma_x. For each alpha, the same temporal-correlation classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was evaluated from Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), and violation of the classical causal bound was used to certify non-classical causal relations.

alpha_interval_with_observed_nonclassica.description: Swap-angle interval, in radians, over which the partial-swap two-point-measurement experiment exhibited violations of the classical causal inequality, thereby certifying non-classical causal relations.

experiment_description: Noise and coherence characterization of the trapped-ion qubit memory used to model the decay of the two-point-measurement memory-certification signal. The same 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor was operated with qubit manipulation by the addressed 729 nm laser and readout by 397 nm fluorescence. Coherent magnetic-field noise at the 50 Hz mains frequency was actively compensated, while a remaining 100 Hz component was mitigated by dynamical decoupling. The experiment applied echo pulses at 2.5 ms intervals during variable waiting periods. Ramsey experiments were performed over a waiting-time sweep from 0 ms to 200 ms; the Ramsey contrast was measured as a function of waiting time and fitted with an exponential decay model to obtain the effective dephasing time T2 under the applied dynamical-decoupling sequence. The same echo pulse used in the memory sequence was also calibrated to estimate its average pulse fidelity.

effective_coherence_time_t2_ms.description: Effective dephasing time T2 of the trapped-ion qubit under the dynamical-decoupling sequence, obtained from an exponential fit to Ramsey-contrast decay.

single_echo_pulse_average_fidelity.description: Average fidelity of an individual echo pulse used in the dynamical-decoupling sequence for the memory-decay experiment.
